record.paper_title: A Survey on Offline Reinforcement Learning: Taxonomy, Review, and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can offline reinforcement learning use unsupervised reinforcement learning or related techniques to exploit large amounts of unlabeled experience when reward labels are scarce or expensive, while still producing effective downstream policies from static data?

evidence.quote: Finally, a promising future direction for the field is the use of unsupervised RL techniques to leverage large amounts of unlabeled data. In many cases, labeling large datasets with rewards may be costly, especially if these require human supervision [88]. Leveraging diverse unlabeled data in a simple yet effective manner is still an open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the offline reinforcement learning setting in which an agent must learn a policy purely from a fixed dataset of previously collected interactions with a Markov decision process (MDP) M = (S, A, P, r, γ), where S is the state space, A the action space, P(s' | s, a) the transition kernel, r : S × A → ℝ the reward function, and γ ∈ [0, 1) the discount factor. Suppose the available data consists of two parts:

1. A large dataset D_u = {(s_i, a_i, s'_i)} of transitions without reward labels.
2. A small dataset D_l = {(s_j, a_j, r_j, s'_j)} of transitions with reward labels, where |D_l| ≪ |D_u|.

No further interaction with the environment is permitted, and reward labeling is assumed to be costly (e.g., requiring human supervision).

Design and analyze an algorithmic framework that uses unsupervised reinforcement learning techniques (such as representation learning, intrinsic-motivation pretraining, skill or option discovery, or self-supervised dynamics modeling) on D_u, together with the labeled subset D_l, to produce a policy π whose expected discounted return J(π) = 𝔼[∑_{t≥0} γ^t r(s_t, a_t)] in M is provably (or empirically) close to that of the optimal policy learnable from a fully reward-labeled dataset of size |D_u| + |D_l|.

Specifically, formulate sufficient conditions on the unlabeled data distribution, the reward function class, and the learning procedure under which the suboptimality J(π*) − J(π) can be bounded as a function of |D_l|, |D_u|, the coverage of D_u over the state–action space, and a measure of complexity of the reward function, in a way that improves over using D_l alone.
artifact.category_tag: Offline reinforcement learning with unlabeled data
artifact.status_search_result: Leveraging large unlabeled offline datasets together with limited reward-labeled data is an active research direction. Methods such as UDS (Unlabeled Data Sharing) by Yu et al. (2022) and PDS (Provable Data Sharing) by Hu et al. (2023) provide partial progress (zero-reward relabeling, reward pessimism, and theoretical guarantees under coverage assumptions), but a general, simple, and effective framework with tight sample-complexity guarantees remains open.

status_evidence.title: How to Leverage Unlabeled Data in Offline Reinforcement Learning (Yu et al., 2022)
status_evidence.snippet: We propose Reward MisSpecification (UDS) which simply applies zero rewards to unlabeled data, and analyze when this is effective.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists via simple reward-relabeling strategies, but the general problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Provable Reward-Agnostic Preference-Based Offline RL / PDS
status_evidence.snippet: Provides pessimistic reward learning from limited labels and uses it to label large unlabeled offline datasets, with theoretical guarantees under coverage assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work gives provable but assumption-heavy guarantees, indicating the problem is only partially solved.

status_evidence.title: A Survey on Offline Reinforcement Learning: Taxonomy, Review, and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Leveraging diverse unlabeled data in a simple yet effective manner is still an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys list this as an open problem.
